 Lawsuit seeks to delay Southern Indiana election results over voting equipment problems 
 Officials reported voting equipment issues at Jeffersonville High School on Election Day. By WDRB+WAVE Digital Staff Published : Nov. 16, 2026 at 6:10 PM EST | Updated : 25 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LOUISVILLE, Ky. (WDRB+WAVE) — Southern Indiana leaders have filed a lawsuit to stop election officials from certifying the results of a state Senate race after voting equipment problems.
 The issues began at Jeffersonville High School on Election Day, when an electronic poll book used to check in voters malfunctioned and a ballot scanner had to be replaced, according to the Clark County Democratic Party.
 The party said 28 more ballots were cast than voters checked in. It also said the election board reviewed ballot sheets, poll pads and precinct results without permission.
 The board later voted not to recount ballots in the Senate District 45 race, which was decided by fewer than 300 votes.
 “Every person involved in this situation agrees there were significant issues with the election. The voters deserve to have their ballots counted fairly and accurately,” the Clark County Democratic Party said in a statement.
 The lawsuit aims to stop the board from certifying the results until the Recount Commission makes a final decision.
